issue: Must a court apply the Biggers two-step reliability analysis before admitting an in-court identification, or can it admit such an identification without that analysis?
provision: U.S. Const. amend. V (due process); Neil v. Biggers, 409 U.S. 188 (1972); Perry v. New Hampshire, 565 U.S. 228 (2012)

sides.position: Courts must apply the Biggers reliability analysis to decide whether an in-court identification is admissible (per Nunn's argument that recent case law requires it)
cases: United States v. Nunn, No. 24-3512 (8th Cir. 2025)

sides.position: Courts need not apply the Biggers reliability analysis to in-court identifications, in light of Perry v. New Hampshire
cases: United States v. Shumpert, 889 F.3d 488 (8th Cir. 2018)
United States v. Evans, 908 F.3d 346 (8th Cir. 2018)

quote: We have observed that the law is currently unsettled as to whether courts must apply the reliability analysis to admit an in-court identification.
cite: United States v. Raphael Nunn, No. 24-3512 (8th Cir. 2025)
